original_text:
I assume Kellogg is marketing this product towards adults who want a healthy cereal that does not lose its crunch over time. Why? The name is Crunchy Nut. The image on the box contains no cartoon characters. In fact, the box design is rather bland. Other than some text stating that "It's Morning Somewhere" therefore you don't need to wait until tomorrow to enjoy the "perfect blend of sweet and nutty in every crunchy bite", it's a pretty uninspiring package. Not at all for the kids...

Is the cereal tasty? Yeah... I enjoyed it. Though immediately felt the need to workout even harder the next day.

Why? The nutritional information states a serving size (3/4 C) contains 1 g of fat. If you add 1/2 C of skim milk, the fat content goes up. Carbs? 23 g before milk. Fiber? A meager 2 g -- a negligible amount. Protein? 2 g.

Tastes good. Is crunchy, even with milk. But be prepared for that sugar crash late morning.

I don't predict it will be around long. I'd much rather eat a bowl of Honey Nut Cheerios... Similar taste and crunch with additional nutritional benefits.
bart_summary: Tastes good. Crunchy, but not good for you.
keywords: healthy cereal; crunchy milk; lose crunch; crunchy nut; cereal

Ballerina are definitely my favourite cookies. I agree with the other reviewer. They are ridiculously delicious and virtually impossible to share! You just *want* the entire package for yourself.

A couple of years ago, I was so addicted to Ballerina and their sister cookies Singoalla that I could eat one package of each instead of supper. I readily admit that my stomach said "no" to that particular guilty pleasure, so these days I avoid Ballerina, not because they are bad, but for the same reason you avoid a Femme Fatale.

Ballerina are chocolate cookies, and my only complaint is that the chocolate tends to melt, making the cookies a somewhat messy experience...unless you devour them really fast! They might give an entirely new meaning to the expression "a quick snack". Also, the cookie really gets stuck to your teeth, so don't forget a tootbrush if you're planning to eat these.

The other flavour, Singoalla, is raspberry + vanilla, and doesn't melt.

Personally, I recommend both. But don't tell me I didn't warn you...

First off, lemme say that I've been eating sunflower seeds for over half my life. I've had pretty much every brand & flavor out there. For years I was buying the David variety of seeds because they're the most readily available. You can find them in pretty much any local store. And for the most part, I like the David seeds with one exception...too much salt! Going through a bag a day while at work would make my mouth dry and tore up from all the salt.

So I took a chance & ordered a 12 pack of these seeds for a few reasons. First off, they're bacon flavored. What's better than that? NOTHING! Big props to the genius who combined sunflower seeds & bacon. Second, the reviews here are mostly favorable. Third, most of the reviews stated these had much less salt than David seeds. And they're right.

I went through a bag of these seeds yesterday and they did not leave my mouth dried up like David seeds. The seeds are larger than average, but I'm not so sure they're bigger than David jumbo seeds. Nevertheless, if you're used to David seeds, get ready for a big change. The flavor of these seeds are pretty good overall, but very different from David seeds. The bacon flavor is somewhat authentic, but I would like to have a bit more of it in these seeds. It just seems a tad too weak in my opinion.

Overall, I really like these seeds. The resealable bag is a big plus too. I look forward to trying their other varieties.
